title: Key to a relationship the text asserts
statement: In a question meant to show the text was understood, key the answer to a relationship the text asserts, since a single retrievable fact is easy to leak.
detail: The reading project's anti-leak writer rules ask for keys that hinge on a relationship the passage asserts (a cause it names, a contrast it draws, an inference it licenses) rather than a lone retrievable noun, since denser passages make relational keys both natural and harder to leak. For inference and theme items, the rationale must quote the two or more sentences whose combination licenses the inference, with no single-sentence lift.
against: Some in-lesson checks are literal on purpose: a ruling keeps reading checks as retrieval, and whether a literal check must be about the theme's hinge was left open (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0230-late-sept-incidental-findings.qmd`, lines 64-66).
